name: Global Aid Foundation
notes: Mid-sized donor providing $180K annual funding for emergency shelter and medical supply programs across South America. Partnership since 2025. H2 2026 funding ($90K) placed in conditional status by Regional Committee on Feb 12 due to missing Q1 impact report. Documentation deadline March 15 for final committee review March 25. Multiple follow-up emails sent (Jan 28, Feb 3, Feb 18) regarding impact reporting requirements. No response received to recent communications. Relationship health declining - immediate intervention needed to preserve funding.

name: Regional Development Foundation
notes: Mid-sized institutional donor providing $35,000 annually for rural education programs. Quarterly reporting required. Simplified administrative requirements compared to other donors. Mutual exclusivity clause with Global Aid Foundation - cannot co-fund same expense line items. Strong relationship, responsive communication.

name: Humanitarian Alliance
notes: Emergency response fund donor. Q1 2026 allocation $20,000 with $12,500 remaining. No co-funding restrictions. Requires detailed itemized documentation and monthly progress reports. Fast approval process (24-48 hours) for emergency requests. Higher administrative burden but flexible on fund combination.

name: Regional Mobile Health Services
notes: Partner organization coordinating mobile health clinic integration with emergency shelter program. Planning April 15 clinic launch in shelter east wing. Strong relationship with Regional Health Ministry. Equipment procurement timeline locked in. Critical coordination partner for integrated service delivery model.

name: Regional Development Foundation
notes: Major infrastructure grant donor. Approved $25,000 grant for rural water/sanitation projects in Q1 2026. Expected disbursement: mid-January (Jan 20-25). Requires detailed project plans and community partnership verification. Strong relationship, responsive program officer (Michael Chen). Grant perfectly timed to support Phase 2 of emergency water crisis response.

name: Humanitarian Alliance
notes: Regional humanitarian coordination body. Not a direct funder but provides sector intelligence, coordination support, and occasional collaborative funding opportunities. Member organization since 2024. Valuable for networking and staying informed on sector trends. Collaborative Fund opportunities require multi-partner consortiums.

name: Global Aid Foundation
notes: Major institutional donor - $120,000 annual grant supporting emergency shelter construction and community education programs. 3-year partnership history. Grant cycle: January-December. Quarterly informal updates expected, annual formal report required. Site visit scheduled March 8, 2026 to Villa Nueva emergency shelter program. Key relationship - represents 40% of organizational budget. Jennifer Morrison very engaged, appreciates transparency and proactive communication. CONCERN: Last substantive contact December 18, 2025 - over 10 weeks ago. No Q1 update sent despite multiple draft attempts. March 8th site visit at risk due to permit delays but donor not yet notified.

name: Community Development Partners
notes: Small foundation supporting community health education programs. $15,000 annual grant. Minimal reporting requirements - annual narrative report only. Low-maintenance relationship. Last contact: brief email exchange about workshop materials.

name: Regional Health Network
notes: Critical regulatory partner for health program operations. Manages mandatory certification requirements for NGO health workers. Strict policies on attendance and compliance. Current issue: Zhuo needs to obtain certification by Feb 27 (mandatory training) but has scheduling conflict with major donor site visit. Exploring options for temporary program coverage through Ana Rodriguez (certified through 2027) while deferring Zhuo's certification to Q4 2026. Relationship is compliance-focused rather than revenue-generating, but essential for maintaining health program partnerships and Regional Health Ministry permits.

name: Villa Nueva & San Pedro Village Council Coalition
notes: Joint village council coalition formed in response to February 2026 flooding emergency. Represents 127 displaced families across Villa Nueva and San Pedro communities. Emergency relief request submitted February 15: $45,000 total ($18k food, $15k shelter materials, $8k medical/hygiene, $4k water equipment). Urgent timeline - 3 weeks for procurement and distribution. Strong community relationship - both villages are existing program partners with excellent collaboration history.

name: Global Aid Foundation
notes: Major institutional donor. Emergency Fund terms 2026: 85% coverage, $50k max per incident, immediate 48hr approval. RESTRICTIONS: Shelter materials require certified vendor approval, equipment has 60-day reimbursement delay, no admin cost coverage. Reimbursement model: org advances 100%, 30-day reimbursement for food/medical, 60-day for equipment. Currently managing emergency shelter program site visit scheduled March 2026. Strong relationship but high compliance requirements.

name: Regional Development Foundation
notes: Regional donor partner. Emergency Grant 2026: 70% coverage, no maximum limit, requires co-funding (minimum 20% from other source). KEY ADVANTAGE: Direct upfront disbursement within 5 business days - no reimbursement delays. All emergency categories eligible, no vendor restrictions. REPORTING REQUIREMENT: Projects over $40k require detailed quarterly impact reports for 12 months. Flexible terms but lower coverage percentage and mandatory co-funding.

name: Humanitarian Alliance
notes: International humanitarian donor. Emergency Fund 2026: 90% coverage (highest rate), $60k max, immediate approval for pre-qualified partners. RESTRICTIONS: Shelter materials NOT eligible, food capped at $15k, equipment requires 15% org co-payment. Reimbursement model: org advances costs, 90% reimbursement within 15 days of receipt submission (45-day submission window). SITE VISIT REQUIREMENT: Program evaluation team visit within 90 days mandatory. High coverage but significant category restrictions.

name: Río Verde Village Council
notes: Emergency water contamination crisis affecting 200 families (850 individuals). Request: $8,000 for water purification system and temporary distribution. Regional Development Foundation hard deadline: January 25, 2026. Health impact: 15 waterborne illness cases reported. HIGH URGENCY - public health emergency risk.

name: Santa Rosa Community Education Committee
notes: School roof repair request for Santa Rosa Elementary. Request: $4,500 for roof repair and temporary waterproofing. Affects 75 students - three classrooms unusable during rain. Global Aid Foundation rolling review (4-6 weeks processing). MEDIUM URGENCY - educational disruption but manageable 3-4 week timeline.

name: Alto Paraíso Health Clinic
notes: Medical supply shortage due to respiratory infection surge. Request: $6,000 for antibiotics, diagnostic supplies, PPE, and first aid. Serves 120 families. Humanitarian Alliance flexible timeline (6-8 weeks standard). MEDIUM URGENCY - critical cases manageable through hospital referrals but creates community hardship.

name: Río Verde Village Council
notes: 6-year partnership history. Strong trust relationship. Community of 200 families (~850 people). Previous collaboration on education and infrastructure projects. Emergency request January 2026: water contamination crisis requiring $8,500 for purification systems and bottled water distribution. 72-hour health-critical timeline. High consequence urgency - irreversible health harm potential for vulnerable populations.

name: Santa Rosa Community Education Committee
notes: 3-year partnership. Facility hosts Aid and Education literacy programs (45 adult learners weekly). Emergency request January 2026: school roof collapse requiring $7,200 for structural repair. Affects 180 children. Safety hazard - engineers warn of complete collapse risk. 10-day repair timeline recommended. Medium-term relationship, moderate trust depth compared to longer partnerships.

name: Alto Paraíso Health Clinic
notes: 4-year partnership on integrated maternal health and nutrition education programs. Emergency request January 2026: medical supply shortage requiring $6,800. Affects 35 pregnant women in prenatal care. Service disruption rather than immediate health crisis - can maintain minimal services for ~2 weeks with rationing. Government resupply delayed until late February. Strong professional relationship focused on program quality.

name: Villa Nueva Community Mechanics Cooperative
notes: Community partner relationship - not commercial vendor. Mateo Rivera is trusted community mechanic who has provided vehicle assistance as neighbor support. January 2026: helped with VEH-003 alternator repair, declined payment, accepted thank-you gift (coffee and school supplies, $45). Relationship equity: POSITIVE. Important to maintain appropriate reciprocity balance and not over-rely on goodwill. Mateo keeps Toyota Land Cruiser parts and knows local terrain well. His support reflects strong community trust in our organization's mission.

name: PAHO Regional Health Network
notes: Pan American Health Organization regional coordination body. Key partner for health sector policy updates, regulatory standards, and coordination opportunities. Launching South American Rural Health Coordination Hub in March 2026 - potential for improved resource sharing and reduced operational duplication. Newsletter indicates new cold chain requirements for medical supply distribution (effective March 1) and new grant opportunities through Regional Development Foundation for infrastructure improvements.

name: Rural Health Coalition
notes: Regional NGO coordination network providing sector intelligence and partnership facilitation. Q1 2026 update highlights: harmonized medical waste disposal requirements across Peru/Bolivia/Ecuador (effective April 2026), potential partnership with Regional Mobile Health Services (CUS-114) for mobile clinic cost-sharing (30-40% operational savings), and Villa Nueva & San Pedro Village Council Coalition interest in hosting regional coordination meeting. Strong alignment with our operational areas and existing community relationships.

name: Community Development Network
notes: Sector network focused on rural community development programs. January bulletin highlighted: Humanitarian Alliance (CUS-113) expanding emergency relief to include health infrastructure funding, updated permit requirements for temporary facilities in Peru (directly relevant to our shelter program delays), and Community Development Partners (CUS-115) offering technical assistance on community-led health education models. Valuable source for grant intelligence and regulatory updates.

name: Regional Medical Supplies International
notes: Preferred vendor for emergency medical supplies since 2025. Competitive pricing with NGO discounts. Reliable delivery timelines (3-4 weeks standard). Non-refundable payment policy after production begins (24 hours post-payment). Previous orders: $8,400 (Nov 2025), $12,200 (Jan 2026). Good relationship, responsive to urgent requests.

name: San Miguel Regional Government - Permit Coordination Office
notes: Municipal government permit coordination office. Isabella Vargas is key informal contact who provides early warning on processing delays and bureaucratic challenges. Has been helpful in navigating permit processes for multiple projects. Relationship built on transparency and proactive communication. Currently coordinating emergency shelter construction permit - official timeline shows 45 days but informal intelligence suggests 60-70 days due to environmental assessment backlog from flood damage response. Isabella suggested exploring Policy Directive 2024-08 for parallel processing pathway.

name: Regional Health Ministry - Emergency Infrastructure Review
notes: Regional health ministry department responsible for health approvals on construction projects. Dr. Patricia Ruiz manages emergency infrastructure review division. Knowledgeable about Policy Directive 2024-08 which provides provisional approval pathway for emergency humanitarian projects. Standard processing: 14 business days after environmental clearance. Provisional processing: 7 business days with emergency designation, allows parallel processing with environmental assessment. Critical partner for emergency shelter program permit navigation.

name: Villa Nueva Builders
notes: Primary contractor for emergency shelter construction program. Experienced with San Miguel Regional Government permit processes. Mentioned crew scheduling constraints if construction delayed beyond March 10.

name: Medical Supplies International

Payment terms: Net 30 days.

name: Humanitarian Alliance Emergency Fund
notes: Emergency response specialist donor.
